title: The Science of Happiness: Can It Be Measured?
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and over the past few weeks, we’ve had quite a few heavy topics: Roman tyrants, hijackings, and American criminals.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，在过去的几周里，我们探讨了相当多沉重的话题：罗马暴君、劫机事件和美国罪犯。

sentences.en: So today we’re talking about something completely different: happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们来聊一个完全不同的话题：幸福。

sentences.en: It’s something we all want to be; it’s something that we all can be, but what does happiness really mean?
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有人都想拥有的状态，也是我们所有人都能拥有的状态，但幸福究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: Can it ever be truly measured, and what, according to the Global Happiness Report, really makes a person happy?.
sentences.zh: 它真的能被准确衡量吗？根据《全球幸福感报告》，究竟是什么让一个人感到快乐？

sentences.en: OK then, let's talk about happiness.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就来聊聊幸福。

sentences.en: Dictionaries are sometimes pretty useless.
sentences.zh: 字典有时其实挺没用的。

sentences.en: If you look up “happiness” in a dictionary, it’ll probably say something like “the state of being happy”.
sentences.zh: 如果你在字典里查“happiness”（幸福），它大概会解释为“快乐的状态”。

sentences.en: So you look up “happy”, and it’ll say something like “feeling or showing pleasure or contentment”, or “a state of well-being”.
sentences.zh: 于是你去查“happy”（快乐的），它又会解释为“感到或表现出愉悦或满足”，或者是“一种福祉状态”。

sentences.en: And there isn’t much reason to look up the definition of “happy”, at least in a monolingual dictionary.
sentences.zh: 而且，至少在单语字典里，我们也没什么必要去查“happy”的定义。

sentences.en: I know what it means, you know what it means, from an office on the 90th floor of a skyscraper in Tokyo to a Kalahari Bushman, we might have different words for it, but we know what it means.
sentences.zh: 我知道它是什么意思，你也知道它是什么意思，无论是东京摩天大楼第 90 层的办公室里的人，还是卡拉哈里沙漠的布须曼人，我们对它可能有不同的称呼，但我们都明白它代表着什么。

sentences.en: It, of course, means different things to different people; different things make different people happy, there are different types of happiness, and something that makes one person happy might make another person sad.
sentences.zh: 当然，对不同的人来说，它意味着不同的事物；不同的事物会让不同的人快乐，幸福也有不同的类型，能让一个人快乐的事物可能会让另一个人感到悲伤。

sentences.en: What is universal is that happiness is something humans, throughout history, have always sought.
sentences.zh: 但普遍的共识是，幸福是人类在整个历史长河中一直在追求的东西。

sentences.en: Happiness as a goal in itself might be more of a recent ideal, but it seems reasonable to suppose that even early hunter-gatherer communities tens of thousands of years ago would have pursued activities that would have brought them happiness, whether that was sitting around a fire and eating a roasted rabbit together, or painting animals on the walls of caves and telling stories to their children.
sentences.zh: 把幸福本身当作一个目标可能是一个比较现代的理想，但可以合理推测，甚至在几万年前的早期狩猎采集社群中，人们也会追求能带给自己快乐的活动，不管是围坐在火堆旁一起吃烤兔子，还是在岩壁上画动物并给孩子们讲故事。

sentences.en: One can imagine that a caveman, his belly full, his partner and children singing songs around him, his face warmed by the sun setting in the west, and just about to retire to his cave for the evening, might have thought, “life is good”.
sentences.zh: 我们可以想象这样一个画面：一个原始人，肚子吃得饱饱的，伴侣和孩子们在他身边唱歌，夕阳的余晖温暖着他的脸庞，正准备回山洞过夜，他当时心里可能会想：“生活真美好。”

sentences.en: Perhaps he would even have declared something along the lines of “I am happy”.
sentences.zh: 也许他甚至会发出“我很幸福”之类的感慨。

sentences.en: Fast forward to the modern era, and we have scientists, statisticians, economists and even governments trying to measure happiness, using it as a yardstick for the well-being of a country, as an alternative to metrics like GDP, Gross Domestic Product.
sentences.zh: 快进到现代，我们有科学家、统计学家、经济学家甚至政府，他们试图用幸福来衡量一个国家的福祉，将其作为国内生产总值（GDP）等指标的替代方案。

sentences.en: So, can happiness really be measured? And before we can measure it, we need to ask: what exactly are we measuring?
sentences.zh: 那么，幸福真的能被衡量吗？在我们测量它之前，我们需要先问：我们到底在测量什么？

sentences.en: Is happiness the fleeting pleasure of a slice of rich chocolate cake, or a glass of wine after a long day at work?
sentences.zh: 幸福是吃一块浓郁巧克力蛋糕时的短暂愉悦，还是工作了一整天后喝上一杯红酒的快乐？

sentences.en: Is it the satisfaction we might get after completing something difficult?
sentences.zh: 是完成一件难事后获得的满足感吗？

sentences.en: A long run, or having a conversation in English that you might have thought you never could?
sentences.zh: 比如长跑，或者用英语进行了一场你以前觉得绝对做不到的对话？

sentences.en: Is it the longer-term satisfaction of a life well lived, someone looking back on their life and thinking, “I am proud of myself”?
sentences.zh: 是回顾一生时觉得不虚此生、心想“我为自己感到骄傲”的那种长期满足感吗？

sentences.en: Is it meaning, purpose, joy, contentment, or all of those things?
sentences.zh: 是意义、目标、快乐、满足，还是所有这些的总和？

sentences.en: Psychologists often distinguish between two broad types of happiness: hedonic happiness, which is about pleasure and the absence of pain, and something called eudaimonic happiness, which is about purpose, growth, and living in line with your values.
sentences.zh: 心理学家通常将幸福大致分为两种类型：享乐型幸福（hedonic happiness），它关乎快乐和痛苦的消除；以及所谓的实现型幸福（eudaimonic happiness），它关乎人生目标、个人成长以及践行价值观的生活方式。

sentences.en: This is actually something that goes all the way back to Aristotle, the 4th-century BC Greek Philosopher who spent considerable time addressing the question of happiness.
sentences.zh: 这实际上可以追溯到亚里士多德，这位公元前 4 世纪的古希腊哲学家曾花大量时间探讨幸福的问题。

sentences.en: Now, Aristotle didn’t exactly split happiness into two categories the way modern psychologists do.
sentences.zh: 不过，亚里士多德并没有像现代心理学家那样把幸福明确分成两类。

sentences.en: His focus was on eudaimonia, which is often translated as “flourishing”, living a virtuous life in line with your values.
sentences.zh: 他的重点是“eudaimonia”，通常被翻译为“繁盛”，也就是过一种符合你价值观的有德行的生活。

sentences.en: He did talk about hedone, or pleasure, but he saw it as just one part of a good life, not equal to eudaimonia.
sentences.zh: 他的确谈到了“hedone”或享乐，但他认为这只是美好生活的一部分，不等同于“eudaimonia”。

sentences.en: Modern psychology has borrowed and adapted these ideas into what we now call hedonic and eudaimonic happiness.
sentences.zh: 现代心理学借鉴并调整了这些理念，演变成了我们现在所说的享乐型幸福和实现型幸福。

sentences.en: And then there’s an even more modern addition: what researchers call subjective well-being.
sentences.zh: 此外还有一个更现代的补充：研究人员所称的主观幸福感（subjective well-being）。

sentences.en: That’s a catch-all term that usually combines three things: how satisfied you are with your life overall, how much positive emotion you experience, and how much negative emotion you experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一个涵盖全面的术语，通常结合了三件事：你对总体生活的满意度、你体验到多少积极情绪，以及你体验到多少消极情绪。

sentences.en: In other words, it’s to do with how happy you feel.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它与你的幸福感有多强有关。

sentences.en: Because, at the end of the day, that’s the only thing that matters, your perception of your own happiness.
sentences.zh: 因为说到底，唯一重要的事情就是你对自己幸福的感知。

sentences.en: The caveman sitting around a fire 50,000 years ago wasn’t thinking, “I wish I had a flat screen TV”, and there are plenty of people today who have plenty of things that theoretically make a person happy–a nice house, a secure job, a loving family–yet for whatever reason, they don’t feel satisfied themselves.
sentences.zh: 5 万年前围坐在火堆旁的原始人并没有在想“我要是有一台平板电视就好了”，而今天有很多人，他们拥有理论上能让人快乐的一切——漂亮的房子、稳定的工作、充满爱的家庭——但出于某种原因，他们自己就是觉得不满足。

sentences.en: So, even before we attempt to measure it, defining what we are measuring, what happiness is, is not exactly easy.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们试图去衡量它之前，先界定我们到底在测量什么、究竟什么是幸福，这绝对不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: Now, one of the first attempts to measure happiness came in the late 18th century, with the father of the Utilitarian movement, Jeremy Bentham.
sentences.zh: 最早尝试衡量幸福的人之一出现在 18 世纪末，他就是功利主义运动的鼻祖杰里米·边沁（Jeremy Bentham）。

sentences.en: He tried to mathematically calculate happiness, and his equation was based on subtracting painful activities from pleasurable ones.
sentences.zh: 他试图用数学方法计算幸福，他的公式基于用快乐的活动减去痛苦的活动。

sentences.en: It was slightly more complicated than this, and activities were split up into seven factors: Intensity, Duration, Certainty, Proximity, Fecundity, Purity, and Extent.
sentences.zh: 实际情况稍微复杂一点，活动被细分为七个因素：强度、持续时间、确定性、邻近性、多产性、纯粹性和范围。

sentences.en: Now isn’t the time to go into all of these, and we do actually have a standalone episode on Jeremy Bentham – it’s episode number 116 – but the point is that it was an early attempt to account for the fact that pleasure and pain have different qualities.
sentences.zh: 现在不是深入探讨所有这些因素的时候，我们其实有一期专门讲杰里米·边沁的独立节目——第 116 期——但重点是，这是早期为了说明“快乐和痛苦具有不同品质”而做出的尝试。

sentences.en: In other words, the pleasure you might get from eating an apple, let’s say, was worth less than the pain of being locked up in prison and tortured for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，比方说，吃苹果带来的快乐，其价值小于被关在监狱里折磨 10 年所承受的痛苦。

sentences.en: And the pleasure of knowing that you had saved the lives of tens of thousands of children was worth more than the pain of stubbing your toe.
sentences.zh: 而知道自己拯救了数万名儿童生命的快乐，其价值大于脚趾头撞到桌角带来的痛苦。

sentences.en: So Bentham was one of the first to dream of quantifying happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以边沁是第一批梦想将幸福量化的人之一。

sentences.en: But his calculus stayed mostly theoretical.
sentences.zh: 但他的计算方法大多停留在理论层面。

sentences.en: After all, if we assume that his weightings and calculations were 100% correct, which they surely were not, then the process of calculating individual happiness would have been so long and complicated that it would firstly have been impractical, and secondly would have taken so long that its subject would no doubt have become quite unhappy while it was taking place.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果我们假设他的权重和计算是 100% 正确的（这显然不可能），那么计算个人幸福的过程将会如此漫长和复杂，以至于首先它不切实际，其次它会耗费太长时间，以至于当事人在计算过程中毫无疑问就已经变得很不快乐了。

sentences.en: It wasn’t until the 20th century that psychologists began developing practical tools – surveys, scales, and experiments – to try to measure how happy people really were.
sentences.zh: 直到 20 世纪，心理学家才开始开发实用的工具——调查问卷、量表和实验——来试图衡量人们究竟有多快乐。

sentences.en: And the most common tool, even today, is perhaps the simplest: the survey.
sentences.zh: 而最常用的工具，即使在今天，也可能是最简单的：问卷调查。

sentences.en: You’ve almost certainly seen questions like these before: “On a scale of 1 to 10, how satisfied are you with your life as a whole?”
sentences.zh: 你几乎肯定以前见过类似的问题：“从 1 到 10 分，你对自己的整体生活有多满意？”

sentences.en: “Taking all things together, would you say you are very happy, quite happy, not very happy, or not at all happy?”
sentences.zh: “综合各方面来看，你会说自己非常快乐、相当快乐、不太快乐，还是一点也不快乐？”

sentences.en: These so-called life satisfaction questions are the backbone of most happiness research.
sentences.zh: 这些所谓的对生活满意度的提问是绝大多数幸福研究的基石。

sentences.en: They are simple, easy to administer across large populations, and when you add them up, you can start to compare one country to another, or track changes over time.
sentences.zh: 它们很简单，易于在广大基数的人群中实施，而且当你把它们汇总起来时，你就可以开始在不同国家之间进行比较，或者追踪随时间推移而发生的变化。

sentences.en: Now, surveys like this are neat, but they have a big limitation: they rely on people remembering and summarising their happiness.
sentences.zh: 这类调查虽然很整洁，但它们有一个很大的局限性：它们依赖于人们对幸福的记忆和总结。

sentences.en: Psychologists know that memory is unreliable: we tend to overemphasise the highs and lows, and undercount the ordinary moments.
sentences.zh: 心理学家知道记忆是不可靠的：我们往往会过度夸大高潮和低谷，而忽视平常的时刻。

sentences.en: This is sometimes referred to as the “peak–end rule”: when people recall an experience, they mostly remember the most intense moment, the “peak”, and how it concluded, the “end”.
sentences.zh: 这有时被称为“峰终定律”：当人们回忆一段经历时，他们主要记得的是最激烈的时刻（即“峰”），以及它如何结束（即“终”）。

sentences.en: You sort of forget the bits in the middle.
sentences.zh: 中间的那些片段你基本上都忘了。

sentences.en: So if you really want to capture happiness more accurately, you need to measure it in the moment, rather than asking people to remember it later.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你真的想更准确地捕捉幸福，你需要即时去衡量它，而不是事后让人们去回忆。

sentences.en: Obviously, this is more complicated, but it is possible.
sentences.zh: 显然，这更复杂，但这是可行的。

sentences.en: That’s where a method called Experience Sampling comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“体验采样法”（Experience Sampling）派上用场的时候了。

sentences.en: This involves pinging people at random times of the day, with a text, an app notification, or even a beeper back in the 1980s, and asking: “How are you feeling right now?
sentences.zh: 这种方法包括在一天中的随机时间给人们发送短信、应用通知，或者在 20 世纪 80 年代使用寻呼机，然后询问：“你现在感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: What are you doing? Who are you with?” The idea is that, by collecting hundreds or thousands of these little snapshots, you can build up a far more realistic picture of what makes people happy.
sentences.zh: 你在做什么？你和谁在一起？”其核心理念是，通过收集成百上千个这样的小快照，你可以拼凑出一幅更真实的画面，了解究竟是什么让人快乐。

sentences.en: And Experience Sampling studies have found some fascinating patterns.
sentences.zh: 体验采样研究已经发现了一些迷人的规律。

sentences.en: People tend to report being happiest when they’re socialising, exercising, or engaged in activities that give them a sense of flow, that feeling of being completely absorbed in what they’re doing.
sentences.zh: 人们往往报告说，当他们在社交、锻炼，或者从事能带给自己“心流”体验的活动时是最快乐的，那种完全沉浸在手头事情中的感觉。

sentences.en: The situations in which they tend to be least happy are probably unsurprising: commuting, working in stressful conditions, or when they’re ill.
sentences.zh: 他们最不快乐的场景可能并不令人意外：通勤、在压力山大的环境下工作，或者生病的时候。

sentences.en: If you are listening to this with a cold on a crowded commuter train, well, you’re probably feeling a bit rubbish.
sentences.zh: 如果你是在一辆拥挤的通勤列车上感冒着听这期节目，嗯，你大概会觉得自己有点糟糕。

sentences.en: Now, self-reported happiness surveys, even these”experience sampling”-style ones, only take us so far.
sentences.zh: 自我报告的幸福感调查，哪怕是这种“体验采样”风格的调查，也只能帮我们到这里。

sentences.en: Scientists have also looked at physiological measures: heart rate variability, levels of the stress hormone cortisol, and even patterns of brain activity.
sentences.zh: 科学家们还研究了生理指标：心率变异性、压力荷尔蒙皮质醇的水平，甚至是脑电波活动的模式。

sentences.en: Neuroscientists have found that certain regions of the brain light up when people report feeling happy.
sentences.zh: 神经科学家发现，当人们报告感到快乐时，大脑的某些区域会被点亮。

sentences.en: When we feel happy, there are clear physiological changes and measuring these kinds of changes is the most accurate way to measure happiness, theoretically speaking, at least.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到快乐时，会有明显的生理变化，从理论上讲，测量这些变化是衡量幸福最准确的方法。

sentences.en: But while these methods can be incredibly precise in a lab, they’re expensive, invasive, and not exactly practical for large populations.
sentences.zh: 但虽然这些方法在实验室里可以做到极其精准，它们价格昂贵、具有侵入性，对于庞大的人口基数来说并不切实际。

sentences.en: In recent years, researchers have tried a different approach altogether: big data.
sentences.zh: 近年来，研究人员尝试了一种完全不同的方法：大数据。

sentences.en: By analysing billions of words on social media, or even the emotional tone of song lyrics, they attempt to track collective happiness in real time.
sentences.zh: 通过分析社交媒体上的数十亿个单词，甚至是歌曲歌词的情感基调，他们试图实时追踪集体幸福感。

sentences.en: One famous study found that people’s tweets tended to be more positive in the morning, dip during the workday, and then rise again in the evening.
sentences.zh: 一项著名的研究发现，人们的推文在早晨往往更积极，在工作期间会下降，然后在晚上再次上升。

sentences.en: Hardly surprising, perhaps. Another tracked changes in national mood based on how cheerful or gloomy song lyrics became over the course of decades.
sentences.zh: 这或许并不令人意外。另一项研究则根据几十年间歌曲歌词变得欢快还是沮丧，来追踪国家情绪的变化。

sentences.en: Interesting from the point of view of measuring the happiness of a wider population over time, but not particularly helpful when it comes to more granular measures.
sentences.zh: 这对于从长远角度衡量更广泛人群的幸福感很有趣，但在进行更细致的测量时并不是特别有用。

sentences.en: So from smartphones to surveys, saliva samples to social media, there are now dozens of different ways to try to measure happiness.
sentences.zh: 因此，从智能手机到问卷调查，从唾液样本到社交媒体，现在有几十种不同的方法试图来衡量幸福。

sentences.en: None of these is perfect, but there has been enough research into the subject over the course of several decades that there are some interesting themes and trends that researchers have seen about what makes someone happy, or not.
sentences.zh: 这些方法都不是完美的，但经过几十年的相关研究，研究人员发现了一些有趣的主题和趋势，关乎是什么让人快乐，或是不快乐。

sentences.en: Some of these will not be surprising; others might be.
sentences.zh: 其中一些不会让人感到意外，另一些则可能会。

sentences.en: One of the clearest findings is that money matters, but only up to a point.
sentences.zh: 最明确的发现之一是金钱很重要，但只在一定程度上重要。

sentences.en: When people are struggling to meet their basic needs, more money reliably increases happiness.
sentences.zh: 当人们难以满足基本需求时，更多的钱确实能可靠地增加幸福感。

sentences.en: The difference between living on two dollars a day and ten dollars is enormous.
sentences.zh: 靠每天两美元生活和靠十美元生活有着巨大的区别。

sentences.en: But once you reach a certain level of comfort, the effect flattens out.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你达到了某个舒适的水平，这种边际效应就会趋于平缓。

sentences.en: Going from an income of €10,000 a year to €20,000 makes a big difference.
sentences.zh: 年收入从 1 万欧元增加到 2 万欧元会有很大的不同。

sentences.en: But going from €100,000 to €200,000? Much less so.
sentences.zh: 但从 10 万欧元增加到 20 万欧元呢？影响就小得多了。

sentences.en: Another theme is the importance of social connections.
sentences.zh: 另一个主题是社会联系的重要性。

sentences.en: Time and time again, the research shows that people who feel they can rely on friends, family, or their community report higher levels of happiness.
sentences.zh: 研究一次又一次地表明，那些觉得自己可以依赖朋友、家人或社区的人报告的幸福感水平更高。

sentences.en: Loneliness, on the other hand, is one of the strongest predictors of unhappiness.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，孤独感是不幸福感的最强预测指标之一。

sentences.en: During the Covid-19 pandemic, when isolation was forced on much of the world, surveys found sharp declines in happiness, especially among younger people.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情期间，当世界上大部分地区被迫处于孤立状态时，调查发现幸福感急剧下降，尤其是年轻人。

sentences.en: Spending time with other people, perhaps unsurprisingly, is positively correlated with self-reported happiness.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，花时间与他人相处与自我报告的幸福感呈正相关。

sentences.en: And the worrying thing is that, across much of the world, people are reporting spending more and more time alone.
sentences.zh: 令人担忧的是，在世界大部分地区，人们报告说自己花在独处上的时间越来越多。

sentences.en: One of the markers of this is “eating alone”.
sentences.zh: 这其中的一个标志就是“独自吃饭”。

sentences.en: According to the 2025 World Happiness Report, “In 2023, roughly 1 in 4 Americans reported eating all of their meals alone the previous day – an increase of 53% since 2003.”
sentences.zh: 根据《2025年世界幸福报告》，“在 2023 年，大约有四分之一的美国人报告说他们在前一天独自吃掉了所有的饭菜——自 2003 年以来增长了 53%。”

sentences.en: And in the same report, household size is positively correlated with happiness, up to a point at least.
sentences.zh: 在同一份报告中，家庭规模与幸福感呈正相关，至少在一定程度上是这样。

sentences.en: According to the report, “In Mexico and Europe, a household size of four to five predicts the highest levels of happiness.
sentences.zh: 根据该报告，“在墨西哥和欧洲，四到五人的家庭规模预示着最高水平的幸福感。”

sentences.en: Couples who live with at least one child, or couples who live with children and members of their extended family, have especially high average life satisfaction.”
sentences.zh: 与至少一个孩子同住的伴侣，或者与孩子以及大家庭成员同住的伴侣，平均生活满意度尤其高。

sentences.en: But the report goes on to acknowledge that people who live in very large households do report lower levels of happiness, but this is probably due to lower levels of economic satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 但报告接着承认，住在非常大家庭里的人确实报告较低的幸福感，但这可能是由于经济满意度较低所致。

sentences.en: Or to put it another way, it might be nice to live with lots of people, but not if you have to queue for 1 hour for a shower every day and there’s only one loaf of bread to feed 15 people.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，跟很多人住在一起可能挺好，但如果你每天必须排队 1 个小时才能洗澡，而且只有一条面包来喂饱 15 个人，那就另当别论了。

sentences.en: There’s also the role of trust. Countries where people believe that others can be trusted, that institutions are fair, and that corruption is relatively low, tend to report higher levels of wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 信任的作用也不容忽视。人们相信他人值得信任、机构是公正的、腐败相对较低的国家，往往报告有更高水平的福祉。

sentences.en: It isn’t just about how much money a country has, but about how fair and safe life feels.
sentences.zh: 这不仅关乎一个国家有多少钱，还关乎生活感觉有多公平、多安全。

sentences.en: To give you a personal example, I live in Sweden, a country that is always towards the top of these happiness reports.
sentences.zh: 举个我个人的例子，我住在瑞典，这个国家在这些幸福感报告中总是名列前茅。

sentences.en: A few months ago, I was coming back from a swimming lesson with my son, and we, or rather I, accidentally left his favourite Spider-Man rucksack on the tram.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，我和儿子上完游泳课回来，我们——或者说是我——不小心把他的蜘蛛侠最爱双肩包落在了有轨电车上。

sentences.en: He was very sad, but I went to the lost and found office the following day, and found that someone had handed it in.
sentences.zh: 他非常伤心，但我第二天去了失物招领处，发现有人把它交上去了。

sentences.en: I had to pay a very small administration fee, and I got it back.
sentences.zh: 我不得不支付了一笔很小的行政管理费，然后把它拿了回来。

sentences.en: This made me happy temporarily, and him very happy when I returned it to him, but it also made me happy on a deeper, more permanent level to think that I live in a place where someone will do that.
sentences.zh: 这让我暂时感到高兴，当我把它还给他时他也非常高兴，但这也让我从更深层次、更持久的层面感到高兴，因为我意识到我生活在一个会有人这么做的地方。

sentences.en: Of course, it might not have been returned, which might have made me unhappy, so if I had been asked if I was happy immediately after I’d been told “sorry, nobody has handed that in”, this might have clouded my mood, which highlights a problem with this self-reporting sampling method.
sentences.zh: 当然，它也可能没有被找回来，那可能会让我不高兴，所以如果在我被告知“对不起，没人交上来”之后立刻问我是否快乐，这可能会影响我的心情，这也凸显了这种自我报告采样方法的一个问题。

sentences.en: But it is a real-life, single data point.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个现实生活中的单一数据点。

sentences.en: And in fact, this year’s Global Happiness Report made this sensation a core focus.
sentences.zh: 事实上，今年的《全球幸福报告》将这种感受作为核心关注点。

sentences.en: One of the things they tracked was almost exactly this: how likely respondents believed it was that a dropped wallet would be returned, depending on whether it was found by a neighbour, a stranger, or a police officer.
sentences.zh: 他们追踪的事情之一几乎正是这一点：受访者认为丢了钱包被找回的可能性有多大，这取决于它是被邻居、陌生人还是警察捡到。

sentences.en: What they found was a definite trend: the more likely someone thought someone else was to do them a good deed, such as returning their lost wallet, the more likely they were to say that they were happy.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了一个明确的趋势：一个人越是认为别人会对自己做善事（比如归还他们丢失的钱包），他们就越倾向于说自己是快乐的。

sentences.en: There were exceptions, of course. Costa Rica is the sixth-happiest country in the world, on a self-reported basis, but comes 128th in terms of trust in a stranger to return a wallet.
sentences.zh: 当然也有例外。哥斯达黎加按自我报告计算是世界上第六快乐的国家，但在相信陌生人会归还钱包方面排名第 128 位。

sentences.en: And Iran is the 99th happiest country in the world, so towards the bottom of the scale, but Iranians were the 2nd most likely people to say that a stranger would return their wallet.
sentences.zh: 而伊朗是世界上第 99 快乐的国家，处于量表底部，但伊朗人却是第二大最有可能说陌生人会归还钱包的人群。

sentences.en: There are exceptions, but there was a strong overall trend.
sentences.zh: 虽然存在例外，但总体趋势非常强烈。

sentences.en: And interestingly enough, this report compared the data on expected wallet return with data on other acts of “caring” for fellow citizens, such as donating to charity, volunteering, or helping a stranger.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这份报告将关于“预期钱包被归还”的数据与关于为同胞提供其他“关怀”行为（如向慈善机构捐款、做志愿者或帮助陌生人）的数据进行了对比。

sentences.en: There was a general trend whereby people in countries ranked higher on these “caregiving” scores reported having higher levels of happiness.
sentences.zh: 总体趋势是，在这些“关怀指数”上排名更高的国家的人们报告拥有更高水平的幸福感。

sentences.en: But the trend was much more defined for the countries that ranked highest on the “care receiving” metrics.
sentences.zh: 但对于在“接受关怀”指标上排名最高的国家来说，这种趋势要明显得多。

sentences.en: To put it another way, yes, caring for others tends to have a positive effect on happiness, but the effect isn’t as great as living in a country where you expect others to care for you.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，是的，关心他人往往会对幸福产生积极影响，但这种影响不如生活在一个你期望别人关心你的国家里那么大。

sentences.en: Interesting, right? Now, to wrap things up, there is unquestionably more to happiness than believing a stranger is going to return your wallet, or in my case, your son’s Spider-Man rucksack.
sentences.zh: 很有意思，对吧？好了，总结一下，毫无疑问，幸福的含义远不止相信陌生人会归还你的钱包，或者以我为例，归还你儿子的蜘蛛侠双肩包。

sentences.en: Happiness is messy, complicated, and impossible to pin down with complete precision.
sentences.zh: 幸福是凌乱的、复杂的，不可能以完全的精确度去定义。

sentences.en: We can try, and we have got better and better at it.
sentences.zh: 我们可以尝试，而且我们已经在这方面做得越来越好。

sentences.en: And we should keep on trying. After all, to quote one of the original thinkers on the concept of happiness, Aristotle, “Happiness is the meaning and the purpose of life, the whole aim and end of human existence”.
sentences.zh: 我们应该继续尝试。毕竟，借用幸福概念的早期思想家之一亚里士多德的话：“幸福是人生的意义和目的，是人类生存的全部目标和终点。”

sentences.en: OK, that is it for today's episode on the science of happiness.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是今天关于幸福科学的节目的全部内容。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目对你有所启发，让你学到了新的知识。

sentences.en: I’ll put a link to the Global Happiness Report in the show notes, if you’d like to check that out yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你想亲自了解一下，我会在节目文稿中附上《全球幸福报告》的链接。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
